records.label: spacr.illumination.IlluminationCorrector#4
records.source: **clip, and count.** A gain above 1 at the edge of the field can push a near-full-scale pixel past the top of a uint16. Clipping is the only option that keeps the dtype the hook contract requires, but silently clipping real signal is a lie about the data, so every pixel that was *below* full scale before the correction and lands *at* full scale after it is counted and reported. Pixels that were already saturated are not counted: they were destroyed by the microscope, not by this class.
records.context: **clip, and count.** A gain above 1 at the edge of the microscope field of view can push a near-full-scale pixel past the top of a uint16. Clipping is the only option that keeps the dtype the hook contract requires, but silently clipping real signal is a lie about the data, so every pixel that was *below* full scale before the correction and lands *at* full scale after it is counted and reported. Pixels that were already saturated are not counted: they were destroyed by the microscope, not by this class.
records.translation: **recortar e contar.** Um ganho superior a 1 na extremidade do campo de visão do microscópio pode empurrar um pixel quase no máximo da escala para além do topo de um uint16. Recortar é a única opção que preserva o dtype exigido pelo contrato do gancho, mas recortar sinal real em silêncio é uma mentira sobre os dados, pelo que cada pixel que estava *abaixo* do máximo da escala antes da correção e fica *no* máximo depois dela é contado e comunicado. Os pixels que já estavam saturados não são contados: foram destruídos pelo microscópio, não por esta classe.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.data_manager.ConfirmDeleteDialog.done#1
records.source: Both Delete and Cancel come through here and NEITHER sends a close event — ``QDialog.done`` hides the widget — so this, not ``closeEvent``, is where a modal dialog's teardown has to live. Qt aborts the process outright if a running ``QThread`` is destroyed with its owner, and the walk can still be out when the user cancels.
records.context: Both Delete and Cancel come through here and NEITHER sends a close event — ``QDialog.done`` hides the widget — so this, not ``closeEvent``, is where a modal dialog's teardown has to live. Qt aborts the process outright if an executing ``QThread`` is destroyed with its owner, and the walk can still be out when the user cancels.
records.translation: Tanto Eliminar como Cancelar passam por aqui e NENHUM dos dois envia um evento de fecho — ``QDialog.done`` esconde o widget —, pelo que é aqui, e não em ``closeEvent``, que tem de residir o desmantelamento de um diálogo modal. O Qt aborta o processo de imediato se um ``QThread`` em execução for destruído com o seu proprietário, e o percurso pode ainda estar a decorrer quando a pessoa cancela.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.fractal_orbit_gpu#2
records.source: WHY IT IS A SECOND ENTRY RATHER THAN A BACKEND SWITCH. The CPU path jitters four samples ACROSS four frames, which averages four different animation times; a GPU pass can afford the four samples inside one instant. They are not the same picture, so offering them as one option with a hidden backend would mean the same setting drawing two things. "Orbit fold" is taken, so this is "Orbit fold (sharp)" -- descriptive of what actually differs rather than a version number.
records.context: Why it is a second entry rather than a backend switch. The CPU path jitters four samples ACROSS four frames, which averages four different animation times; a GPU pass can afford the four samples inside one instant. They are not the same picture, so offering them as one option with a hidden backend would mean the same setting drawing two things. "Orbit fold" is taken, so this is "Orbit fold (sharp)" -- descriptive of what actually differs rather than a version number.
records.translation: Porque é uma segunda entrada e não um seletor de motor. O percurso em CPU distribui quatro amostras AO LONGO de quatro fotogramas, o que faz a média de quatro tempos de animação diferentes; uma passagem em GPU pode dar-se ao luxo das quatro amostras dentro de um único instante. Não são a mesma imagem, pelo que oferecê-las como uma só opção com um motor escondido significaria a mesma definição a desenhar duas coisas. "Orbit fold" já está ocupado, portanto esta é "Orbit fold (sharp)" — descritiva do que realmente difere, em vez de um número de versão.

records.source: A live view like the other three, and since the shared contract (:class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.preview_contract.LivePreviewContract`) it wears their vocabulary: the same **Run preview** button, the same **Cancel** beside it, and a sentence on the status line whenever it cannot preview. It used to be alone in every one of those columns — its button said "Refresh crops", nothing could be cancelled, and a press with no array loaded did nothing and said nothing.
records.context: A live view like the other three, and since the shared contract (:class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.preview_contract.LivePreviewContract`) it wears their vocabulary: the same **Run preview** button, the same **Cancel** beside it, and a sentence on the status line whenever it cannot preview. It used to be alone in every one of those columns — its button said "Refresh crops", nothing could be cancelled, and a press with no array loaded did nothing and said nothing.
records.translation: Uma vista em direto como as outras três e, desde o contrato partilhado (:class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.preview_contract.LivePreviewContract`), veste o seu vocabulário: o mesmo botão **Run preview**, o mesmo **Cancel** ao lado e uma frase na linha de estado sempre que não consegue pré-visualizar. Antes estava sozinha em cada uma dessas colunas — o botão dizia "Refresh crops", nada podia ser cancelado, e uma pressão sem matriz carregada não fazia nada e nada dizia.

records.label: spacr.schema.ObjectID#5
records.source: ``o<label>`` when the object's type is not stated, or ``<type><label>`` when it is. The type lives *inside* this field rather than beside it so that two :class:`ObjectID` values compare equal exactly when they name the same object — a separate ``objectType`` field would let ``('o7', 'nucleus')`` and ``('nucleus7', None)`` describe one object and compare unequal.
records.context: ``o<label>`` when the object's type is not stated, or ``<type><label>`` when it is. The type lives *inside* this microscope field of view rather than beside it so that two :class:`ObjectID` values compare equal exactly when they name the same object — a separate ``objectType`` microscope field of view would let ``('o7', 'nucleus')`` and ``('nucleus7', None)`` describe one object and compare unequal.
records.translation: ``o<label>`` quando o tipo do objeto não é indicado, ou ``<type><label>`` quando é. O tipo vive *dentro* deste campo, e não ao lado dele, para que dois valores :class:`ObjectID` sejam iguais exatamente quando nomeiam o mesmo objeto — um campo ``objectType`` separado permitiria que ``('o7', 'nucleus')`` e ``('nucleus7', None)`` descrevessem um só objeto e fossem comparados como diferentes.

records.label: spacr.spacrops.stitch_cycle_wells#2
records.source: THE MOSAIC IS OPT-IN. Set ``write_mosaic`` (or its synonym ``mosaic``) to build one. It is off by default because assembling a mosaic raises when too few tiles overlapped to place any, and a plate that cannot be stitched should not become a plate that cannot be organised.
records.context: The stitched image grid is opt-in. Set ``write_mosaic`` (or its synonym ``mosaic``) to build one. It is off by default because assembling a stitched image grid raises when too few microscope image fields overlapped to place any, and a plate that cannot be stitched should not become a plate that cannot be organised.
records.translation: A grelha de imagens cosida é opcional. Defina ``write_mosaic`` (ou o seu sinónimo ``mosaic``) para construir uma. Está desativada por predefinição porque montar uma grelha de imagens cosida lança um erro quando poucos campos de imagem do microscópio se sobrepõem para colocar algum, e uma placa que não pode ser cosida não deve tornar-se uma placa que não pode ser organizada.
